Submitted photo Tulmar Safety Systems Inc. has been selected by Global Affairs Canada to participate in the official Team Canada delegation to the 34th International Defence Industry Exhibition, known as MSPO, in Kielce, Poland, where Canada will serve as the Lead Nation. “Being selected for the Team Canada delegation gives Tulmar an important platform to demonstrate the capabilities that a Canadian designer and manufacturer from Hawkesbury can bring to allied defence,” said Ève Léveillé, Marketing Leader at Tulmar. 200.title: EU Bans Nail Polish Ingredient TPO Over Reproductive Health Concerns
200.summary: Matilda Omonaiye/ The European Union has banned Trimethylbenzoyl Diphenylphosphine Oxide (TPO), a chemical used in some gel nail polishes and other UV-curing nail products, after it was classified as a Category 1B substance toxic to reproduction. The ingredient has therefore been widely used in UV-curing nail gels, builder gels and some hybrid nail products.
200.body: Matilda Omonaiye/ The European Union has banned Trimethylbenzoyl Diphenylphosphine Oxide (TPO), a chemical used in some gel nail polishes and other UV-curing nail products, after it was classified as a Category 1B substance toxic to reproduction. The ingredient has therefore been widely used in UV-curing nail gels, builder gels and some hybrid nail products. An earlier assessment by the EU’s Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety had concluded in 2014 that TPO could be considered safe for use in nail-modelling products at concentrations of up to 5 per cent, while also identifying it as a moderate skin sensitiser.

300.title: Poland to cut middle-class taxes as Tusk targets big business
300.summary: The package is designed to ease the tax burden on Poland’s growing middle class while raising additional revenue from the country’s largest companies and wealthiest taxpayers. Around 3.5 million taxpayers are expected to benefit from the changes, which will raise the personal income tax (PIT) threshold and introduce a new intermediate rate for middle earners.
300.body: The package is designed to ease the tax burden on Poland’s growing middle class while raising additional revenue from the country’s largest companies and wealthiest taxpayers. Around 3.5 million taxpayers are expected to benefit from the changes, which will raise the personal income tax (PIT) threshold and introduce a new intermediate rate for middle earners. New middle-income tax rate The government proposes raising the personal income tax threshold from PLN 120,000 (€27,744) to PLN 130,000 (€30,061) a year. Big corporations to pay more The government acknowledges that the middle-class tax relief will cost the budget several billion zlotys and plans to compensate for the lost revenue through higher taxes on large companies and wealthy individuals.

300.title: After drought, Maine town challenges Poland Spring bid to keep pumping 432,000 gallons a day

300.body: Business After drought, Maine town challenges Poland Spring bid to keep pumping 432,000 gallons a day "I suggest the new ordinance applies to them." by James Nanzo August 19, 2026 share Facebook " target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"> Twitter Link Copied! Photo Credit: Poland Spring One Maine town is pushing back as bottling company Poland Spring seeks permission to continue extracting up to 432,000 gallons of water per day from a local aquifer for another five years, according to news outlet Maine Public. Here's what to know Poland Spring wants to keep using the Cold Spring site in the town of Denmark, Maine, seeking access to as much as 105.1 million gallons of water a year. Poland Spring said it voluntarily reduced withdrawals during drought conditions , but Maine Public reported that its review of monthly data found that January-to-September withdrawals in Denmark were up by nearly 23%.

500.title: OpenAI fortifies advanced AI models to block autonomous cyberattacks
500.summary: OpenAI has strengthened its security models with new safeguards that adapt to their capabilities, reports EP, to ensure they do what is expected of them and prevent new autonomous hacks like the one at Hugging Face.
500.body: OpenAI has strengthened its security models with new safeguards that adapt to their capabilities, reports EP, to ensure they do what is expected of them and prevent new autonomous hacks like the one at Hugging Face. The security incident caused by two OpenAI models in July, which autonomously left an isolated test environment with restricted internet access and hacked the Hugging Face platform to find information that would help them solve one of the tests posed during an evaluation, has prompted a review of the security measures of sophisticated artificial intelligence systems. These efforts include improving reward models and training models to be more honest and reduce behaviors that exploit weaknesses in rewards, evaluators, tools, or oversight. These new measures have been applied not only to Sol or similar models but also to Astra models (upcoming launch), focused on cybersecurity, which in internal evaluations have shown they can achieve critical capabilities.

The study found that 86% of organizations have moved beyond the AI agent pilot stage, yet just 34% say they trust the actions their AI agents are taking. - Advertisement - Among organizations in a state of “agentic chaos” (the bottom quartile for operational readiness across governance, integration, API/MCP management, and other categories), 77% are moving into production anyway. When building the agents themselves, 86% of organisations with agentic control say iPaaS and API management capabilities for building AI agents are important to their readiness, compared with just 58% of those in agentic chaos: the single widest gap Forrester measured in the entire study.
